headline: High: Perplexity’s vendor-hosted browsing can feed unstructured’s file-processing pipeline, creating default-path data leakage and cascading errors; prompt-injection risk is lower but present via shared document content.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Perplexity ingests live web and uploaded document content, and unstructured reads and writes documents in a processing pipeline. If Perplexity outputs attacker-controlled text that unstructured later parses as instructions or metadata, injection is plausible. The pair lacks explicit provenance controls, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Perplexity output is copied into a document that unstructured later parses as structured instructions or metadata.
IF unstructured is configured to trust document text as directives rather than inert content.
mitigations: Add a strict content-sanitization step before handing Perplexity output to unstructured.
Use a delimiter/header that marks all upstream text as untrusted.
Disable any parser mode that interprets embedded instructions.
Review one sample handoff document for instruction-like strings.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between the two agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Perplexity is vendor-hosted and sends queries/documents to api.perplexity.ai and search providers, while unstructured reads local documents and writes processed outputs. In a shared-workspace pairing, sensitive document contents can flow from unstructured into Perplexity’s third-party backend by default, creating exfiltration risk. The interaction is documented only at profile level, so uncertainty remains but does not reduce severity.
conditions: IF unstructured processes sensitive documents that are then sent to Perplexity for search or summarization.
IF both agents operate on the same workspace or file handoff path.
mitigations: Keep sensitive documents out of Perplexity prompts.
Route only redacted excerpts from unstructured to Perplexity.
Store handoff files in a separate non-sensitive workspace.
Verify no secrets appear in the first 200 lines of any shared document.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP/redaction before vendor-hosted calls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Unstructured can read and write files, spawn subprocesses, and install packages; Perplexity can browse and handle uploaded files but cannot write the host filesystem. They can still contend over shared documents or outputs in a common directory, causing overwrite or stale-state issues. Because only one agent has host write, this is conflict-prone but not the highest tier.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory or document set.
IF unstructured writes outputs that Perplexity later re-reads without locking.
mitigations: Assign separate input/output directories per agent.
Use unique filenames with timestamps or UUIDs.
Add a quick file-lock check before writes.
Avoid concurrent runs on the same document set.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Perplexity produces cited answers from live web search, and unstructured is a document-processing pipeline that can consume those outputs as text. If unstructured treats Perplexity’s answer as authoritative, any hallucination or citation error can cascade into downstream extraction or transformation. The pair lacks a built-in verification step, so default-path misuse can cause broad downstream errors.
conditions: IF unstructured ingests Perplexity-generated answers without a verification pass.
IF downstream documents or datasets are produced from those answers.
mitigations: Require a human review step before ingestion.
Keep source URLs alongside extracted claims.
Reject outputs lacking explicit citations.
Compare a small sample against original sources.
requires-engineering: add automated claim verification.

E_compliance.rationale: Perplexity is vendor-hosted with vendor-only egress and handles uploaded documents, while unstructured is a local/containerized processor with allowlisted egress. If regulated or residency-bound data is processed by both, the pair can create a retention/residency mismatch between a third-party SaaS and a local pipeline. The profiles do not show a DPA or residency guarantee, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF regulated documents are sent through Perplexity and then retained or transformed by unstructured.
IF the deployment requires residency or retention controls not documented in either profile.
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from the pair.
Confirm retention settings for Perplexity uploads.
Run unstructured only on de-identified copies.
Document the data flow for audits.
requires-engineering: add residency-aware routing and retention enforcement.
